label: CKD review: Review recent systemic NSAID supply in a patient with previously documented stage 3b, 4 or 5 CKD
title: Review recent systemic NSAID supply in a patient with previously documented stage 3b, 4 or 5 CKD
statement: For an adult outpatient with established CKD, review a systemic NSAID supplied in the three calendar months leading up to the latest date in the record if CKD stage 3b, 4 or 5 was documented at least three calendar months before that date.

plain_summary: For an adult outpatient with established CKD, review a systemic NSAID supplied in the three calendar months leading up to the latest date in the record if CKD stage 3b, 4 or 5 was documented at least three calendar months before that date. Stocks P7 covered non-selective NSAIDs. This Australian adaptation also includes systemic celecoxib and etoricoxib because of their renal effects.

medicine_groups.name: Systemic non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs

ibuprofen: Advil Childrens Pain and Fever 2 to 7 Years
Advil Childrens Pain and Fever 7 to 12 Years
Advil Childrens Pain and Fever Relief 2 to 12 Years
Advil Infants Pain and Fever Relief 3 Months to 2 Years
Nurofen for Children 3 Months to 5 Years

medicine_groups.note: Count oral, rectal and injected NSAIDs, including a named NSAID in a combination product. Exclude topical and ophthalmic preparations and aspirin. Indomethacin is the older spelling of indometacin. Check the form when a brand is shared. Orudis suppositories count. Orudis Gel, Feldene Gel and Voltaren Emulgel do not. If the route is unclear, ask which form was supplied.

needs_facts.what: Stage 3b, 4 or 5 CKD documented at least three calendar months before the latest date in the record
needs_facts.meets: Stage 3b, 4 or 5 CKD documented at least three calendar months before the latest date in the record. A dated qualifying stage entry can establish both CKD and its stage. An unstaged diagnosis date alone does not establish when a qualifying stage was first documented. Missing stage or date allows at most a possible finding.

options.words: The dated record confirms this stage and timing
The records establish that no such stage was documented by the cut-off

needs_facts.meets: CKD was established by the NSAID supply under review. If its timing is uncertain, keep the finding possible unless another fact rules it out.

options.words: CKD was established by the NSAID supply under review
CKD was absent at the NSAID supply under review

rule_for_models: Confirm a finding only in an outpatient aged 18 or older with established CKD. If age is unknown and the other evidence supports review, report at most a possible finding and ask whether the patient was 18 or older at supply. Report a finding for a systemic NSAID supplied in the last three months of the record when CKD stage 3b, 4 or 5 was documented at least three calendar months before review. A later eGFR does not cancel that history. Report no finding if CKD is ruled out, the documented historical stage is below 3b with no qualifying stage, or there is no qualifying supply. Cite the systemic NSAID and the dated CKD evidence that is available. A possible finding for missing stage does not require an eGFR citation. Use the latest date in the record as the review date for both windows. When a recent systemic NSAID is visible and the record neither establishes nor rules out qualifying CKD, report a possible finding. If the qualifying stage or its date is missing, name "Stage 3b, 4 or 5 CKD documented at least three calendar months before the latest date in the record" in the possible finding. An unstaged diagnosis alone cannot date a qualifying stage. A record or pharmacist answer confirming stage 3b, 4 or 5 by the three-month cutoff also establishes CKD by the recent supply.
cannot_be_seen: Dispensing does not establish the dose taken. Kidney results obtained elsewhere, their units and their timing may be missing.
ask_the_gp: Could you review the recent systemic NSAID supply and confirm whether CKD stage 3b, 4 or 5 had been documented at least three months before this review?
